experience_texts: After more than 5.5 years of working in the industry, it’s time!

have been nothing short of incredible. As an engineer, I’ve learned and grown in ways I never imagined. But more than just code, I silently observed: how product managers led, how leaders made decisions, how great products were built. And in that silence, I learned. I evolved. Not just as an engineer, but as someone quietly preparing to build something of their own.
, which started as a passion and now touches nearly 1 million learners. And today, I’ve decided — it’s time to go all in.
I’m calling it a day at
Where next? I’ll be taking up TUF full time (Engineering, Content, and Growth).
I am not getting any younger, and I got to find time for myself. I won’t be putting out any video around this. I’ve never been great at that type of content.
The next video you see from me will be on YouTube, teaching System Design — something I’ve longed to do but never had the time for.

The last 5 years have been intense: 13–14 hours almost every single day. Juggling a full-time job, content creation, and building a startup from scratch. In the process, I’ve let my health slip, distanced myself from people who matter, and ignored the small joys that make life worth living.
Now, as I step into the next phase, on the other side of my 20s, I want to reclaim some of that balance. I still want to grind, but not at the cost of my body, my people, or my peace.

I’m at a stage in life where two roads lie ahead, like many of you will face one day. I’ve chosen the predictable one, just like most of you do at every stage of life: to build what’s already working, to double down on what gives me FINANCIAL stability, freedom, longevity, and above all, allows me to spend each day doing what I love: engineering and teaching.
I leave Google with nothing but gratitude in my heart.
For the culture I thrived in.
I will always look back at this chapter with a smile.
I woke up to 600K on YouTube! Thank you to you all, I am what I am today because of you people.
A parent I met at the
office yesterday made me realize the impact
has created. I want to share a small happy story about yesterday.
I was with my team at the cafeteria when I met and clicked pictures with 10+ people in multiple rounds who had recently joined Google.

Among them, some had their parents around who saw all this from a corner. They came to see the amazing office and were so happy and proud, which was clearly visible on their faces. When I was leaving, one of the fathers came up to me and said he wanted to thank me. He shared how his daughter keeps telling him that she did most of her preparation from my channel.
He also added how they come from a small village, where dreaming big is rare. Yet there he was, standing with his daughter, who was probably 21/22 at most, working at Google, making her father proud.

I've heard a lot of praise, but hearing this from a father meant the world to me. I know if not me, the girl would have learned from somewhere else, but just to feel that I was a part of her journey, helping make her parents proud, gave me an emotional feeling.
We hit 600K today, and this happened yesterday—God's plan, maybe!
At takeUforward as of today, we have
▪️30K+ unique users land on the website daily.
▪️100K+ views on the educational channel daily.
▪️Nearly 100K+ page visits daily on the website.
I started takeuforward all by myself 3 years back. The idea was to create a swimming pool of resources. For the first 2 years, we hardly generated any revenue or views.
In our early days, I recorded my screen and used a 500 rs boya mic to record lectures in a small room, I had very less to invest in a proper setup, hence could not add my face initially.

I was struggling to expand it alone, this is where my school friend decided to join me. He took the YT channel to the next level by creating a website which we wanted to be the go-to point for interview preparation. We still have some distance to travel.

My friend stays behind the camera, but he today single-handedly is responsible for almost every piece of content that you see on the website. I hardly had anything to offer him initially, but he did stick with it during those tough times, and today we are having 30K+ unique live people on our website daily and today we easily make a 7-digit revenue.
All you need is a good founding team or co-founders who are willing to put in that extra yard and build it. Build a team around like-minded people with similar visions.
But it’s not always this easy for everyone to find the right co-founder or founding team members.

I recently got to know about the CoFounder App  app where you can connect with similarly skilled people, and get co-founders, founding members, advisors, and founding interns easily. I liked the manual verification process on the app which keeps authentic and high-quality profiles.
Today due to God's grace, we have a really good set-up, editors, algorithmic content writers, web devs, managers, interns and we are growing steadily.
Check out the CoFounder App  app or share it with your friends who are struggling to build their dream teams!
No matter who you are, you will always want to take this one pic. I was waiting for so long to fulfill this wish of mine, and I finally took one.
Warsaw has been so welcoming, the work from the office environment, the employee treatment, everything has been amazing so far.
Looking forward to having some amazing days here.
I move on to the next chapter of my life, where I will be joining
Warsaw physically, and I am excited about this.
The last 2 years have been amazing in India, but you make tough decisions sometimes that help will you grow as individuals, and this was one of them that I took.
"We’ll meet again. Don’t know where, don’t know when, but I know we’ll meet again, someday"
Team Leadership & Ownership Culture, Growth & User-Centric Strategy and +3 skills
takeUforward is on a mission to build the ONE-STOP platform for every aspiring software engineer - covering everything from DSA and System Design to Core Subjects and Interview Prep.
- Scaled TUF to 1M+ signed-up users with 5M+ monthly visits, purely through word of mouth
- Maintained a strong user rating of 4.83 from learners who’ve subscribed to our offerings
- Built and run a profitable tech-first business with long-term sustainability in mind
- Lead the entire product and tech stack, developed fully in-house.
- Working with a pizza-size team that ships fast and takes complete ownership of what they build
- Focused on delivering a smooth, motivating, and outcome-driven experience that helps engineers stay consistent and grow
We're not just another course site. We're building the platform that every engineer can trust throughout their learning journey.
Building the best Google TV experience for your household.
Recommendations that Raj receives will appear here.
developer • oss contributor (urunc, consul democracy, p4org, dataframe, cilium)
Jeetraj responsibly disclosed a critical TUF+ vulnerability with a clear writeup and video proof.
He helped us improve security despite us having no bounty program. Truly appreciate the professionalism.
Anamika joined our young engineering team during the summer and made an outsized impact while we are building the product from scratch.
- Revamped a complex side panel into a clean, extensible experience the team can iterate on quickly.
- Built Focus Mode, which users loved and which meaningfully improved the user's learning experience.
- Led a POC for our upcoming Debugger Mode, unblocking key technical decisions and informing the roadmap.

What impressed me most was her ability to thrive in a true startup environment: ambiguous problems, fast feedback loops, tight timelines. She asks sharp questions, ships thoughtfully, writes maintainable code, and balances user experience with engineering rigor.

For someone in her 2nd year, her depth, ownership, and product sense are exceptional. I would rehire Anamika in a heartbeat if she is there next summers or going forward any time. Any team looking for a fast learner who takes responsibility and delivers real value would be lucky to have her.
I was presented with an accolade of the "Geek of the Year" from one of the ed-tech website GeeksforGeeks
Stood second in their Coding event which was a part of their annual technical fest.
Secured 67th rank in Kanpur regionals of ACM ICPC 2019-2020
Secured an AIR of 16 in Codevita 2019-20
